question: Why do doctors generally avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives for women with sickle cell disease after childbirth?

options.A: They immediately stop all breast milk production
options.B: They cause permanent changes in maternal voice pitch
options.C: They increase the risk of dangerous blood clots
options.D: They destroy the effectiveness of folic acid supplements

explanation: Correct! Estrogen raises clot risks, and since postpartum mums with sickle cell are already prone to clots, it's best to steer clear.

question: What is the medical term for blood collecting inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pleural effusion
options.B: Hemothorax
options.C: Chylothorax
options.D: Pneumothorax

explanation: You've got this! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest is a hemothorax.

question: When should a community health nurse clean and disinfect a measuring tape?

options.A: Only when it looks visibly dirty
options.B: Once a month during equipment audit
options.C: At the end of each working week
options.D: After every single client use

explanation: Wiping the tape after every patient prevents the spread of skin infections and pathogens between community members. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h6)

question: When is it time to clean and disinfect a portable monitor?

options.A: Whenever the battery runs completely flat
options.B: Only once a week during night shift
options.C: Only if visibly stained with blood
options.D: After every single patient use

explanation: Wiping down the equipment between patients stops germs from spreading and keeps our hospital environment safe.

question: What does the term 'contact time' mean when using a disinfectant?

options.A: The number of hours the nurse wears gloves during the shift
options.B: The time the surface must stay wet with the product to kill germs
options.C: The time it takes for the liquid bottle to completely empty
options.D: The time it takes for the skin to dry after a scrub

explanation: Disinfectants do not work instantly; they require a specific duration of continuous wetness to fully eliminate pathogens. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h4)

question: How do many Nigerian families typically approach end-of-life decisions compared to Western models?

options.A: By leaving all choices entirely to junior hospital staff
options.B: Through a communal approach involving extended family members
options.C: By signing formal living wills upon hospital admission
options.D: By avoiding discussions about death and dying completely

explanation: In many Nigerian and African cultures, health decisions are rarely made alone. They are usually discussed and decided together as an extended family unit.

question: What emotional state best describes the acceptance stage?

options.A: Intense bargaining for extra time with family
options.B: Extreme anger and hostility toward medical providers
options.C: Quiet peace and realistic acknowledgment of mortality
options.D: Joyful celebration of a long life well lived

explanation: Acceptance is marked by a calm, albeit often tired, readiness for the end of life rather than happiness. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why do nurses check kidney function (like serum creatinine) before starting certain first-line ARVs?

options.A: Drugs like tenofovir can affect renal function and require safe dosing
options.B: It proves whether the patient has active tuberculosis infection
options.C: Good kidney function guarantees the patient will never miss a dose
options.D: Kidney tests tell the nurse how many CD4 cells the patient has left

explanation: You're right! Some drugs like Tenofovir can put stress on the kidneys, so checking baseline labs ensures the medication is completely safe for that patient's body.

question: What is the age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

options.A: 5 to 12 years old
options.B: 18 to 25 years old
options.C: 10 to 19 years old
options.D: 13 to 30 years old

explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent bracket as spanning from age 10 through 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses track CD4 T-cell counts regularly during antiretroviral therapy?

options.A: To evaluate the recovery and strength of the immune system
options.B: To predict how much weight the patient will gain
options.C: To decide if the patient needs immediate blood transfusions
options.D: To calculate the exact date the patient was infected

explanation: You've got this! Tracking CD4 counts is like checking the health score of the immune system to see how well it's bouncing back.

question: Why should hospital management always consult frontline ward nurses when planning a new ward layout?

options.A: Nurses know practical workflow details like storage bottlenecks and blind spots
options.B: Nurses will personally fund the construction of the new nursing station
options.C: Nurses are legally required to sign off on all architectural blueprints
options.D: Nurses decide the overall construction budget for the entire hospital

explanation: You are the one working in the space every day! Consulting nurses helps catch practical issues—like where supplies should go—that architects might easily miss.

question: What is the only true cure for preeclampsia?

options.A: Complete bed rest
options.B: High-dose vitamin tablets
options.C: Delivery of the placenta
options.D: Cutting out salt completely

explanation: Because preeclampsia originates from the placenta, bringing the baby and the placenta out into the world is the only way to fully stop the condition.

question: What do we call a normal, smooth, and uncomplicated labour and delivery?

options.A: Placenta praevia
options.B: Eutocia
options.C: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.D: Dystocia

explanation: You've got this! Eutocia is just the medical word for a normal, straightforward delivery, while dystocia means a difficult labour. Easy peasy!

question: What is a key role of water as a solvent in the human body?

options.A: It acts as the main building block for bone tissue.
options.B: It stores excess energy in the liver and muscles.
options.C: It provides calories for immediate muscle movement.
options.D: It allows cellular chemical reactions to take place.

explanation: Water acts as a brilliant mixing bowl (solvent) inside our cells, letting vital chemical reactions happen smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance?

options.A: To continuously track health data and spot where diseases are hiding
options.B: To make cheap medicines for rural clinics
options.C: To diagnose patients with long-term mental illness
options.D: To punish hospitals that miss their cleaning schedules

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on community health trends so we can catch outbreaks before they blow up.

question: Why is couples counseling often recommended when treating sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Because sexual problems usually impact both partners in the relationship
options.B: To legally bind partners to follow the treatment plan
options.C: Because individual therapy is strictly illegal for sexual issues
options.D: To prove which partner is at fault for the problem

explanation: Intimacy is shared between two people. Involving both partners encourages teamwork and open communication, which speeds up healing.

question: Why are drugs like morphine classified under strict schedules even though they have medical uses?

options.A: They carry a high risk of dependence and abuse
options.B: They are extremely expensive to import from abroad
options.C: They can only be administered by specialized surgeons
options.D: They lose their potency very quickly in storage

explanation: Even though they relieve severe pain, strong opioids can easily lead to addiction if not closely monitored. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the pulmonary circuit?

options.A: Delivering nutrients directly to skeletal muscles
options.B: Pumping systemic blood to the lower extremities
options.C: Carrying blood between the heart and the lungs
options.D: Removing waste products from the brain tissue

explanation: The pulmonary circuit specifically handles the transport of blood from the heart to the lungs to pick up oxygen and release carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is a chest X-ray usually done right after a thoracentesis?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of remaining chest fluid
options.B: To check if the rib bones healed from the puncture
options.C: To confirm lung expansion and check for a collapsed lung
options.D: To verify that the heart valves are working normally

explanation: Spot on! An X-ray lets us double-check that the lung expanded nicely and that no air slipped into the chest cavity.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used for animals, while quarantine is used only for humans
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.C: Isolation is done at home, while quarantine is done in a laboratory
options.D: Quarantine requires heavy medication, while isolation requires only rest

explanation: Isolation keeps confirmed infectious patients away from others, whereas quarantine watches people who might have caught the disease during their incubation period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which committee operates closest to individual households in a rural Nigerian setting?

options.A: Village Development Committee
options.B: National Policy Committee
options.C: State Implementation Committee
options.D: Local Government Health Board

explanation: The Village Development Committee is the lowest tier, sitting directly within the community to handle immediate local health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h2)

question: Where should you drop a used needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.A: Inside a puncture-resistant safety box
options.B: Back inside its original plastic wrapper
options.C: In the general office waste basket
options.D: On top of the treatment trolley tray

explanation: Well done! Always drop used sharps straight into a safety box to prevent accidental needle pricks on the ward.

question: Which nutritional issue is especially common during the rapid physical growth of adolescence?

options.A: Scurvy
options.B: Anaemia
options.C: Rickets
options.D: Goiter

explanation: Rapid growth and poor dietary habits make adolescents, especially young females, very prone to developing anaemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: When checking vital signs, why is it better to look at trends over time rather than a single reading?

options.A: Single readings are always completely wrong
options.B: Trends automatically calculate medication doses
options.C: A single reading can miss subtle shifts in a patient's overall condition
options.D: Isolated numbers are illegal to chart

explanation: You got it! Looking at how vitals change over time gives you a much better picture of your patient's stability than just one snapshot.

question: Why should community health nurses pay attention to joblessness as a public health issue?

options.A: It increases chronic stress and mental health disorders
options.B: It directly causes infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: It guarantees immediate physical disability
options.D: It alters human anatomical development in adulthood

explanation: Well done! Lacking work can lead to prolonged stress, anxiety, and depression, which affect overall well-being. Every small step counts! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why can regular hospital IV pumps sometimes cause trouble during a flight?

options.A: Air pressure causes the IV tubing to melt
options.B: Vibration and pressure changes can affect pump accuracy
options.C: Infusion pumps require constant connection to plumbing
options.D: Hospital pumps are too quiet to hear over the engines

explanation: You're doing great! Engine vibrations and shifts in cabin air pressure can mess with standard pumps, so flight nurses use specially calibrated equipment.

question: How can a nurse manager best handle frequent equipment shortages during daily ward activities?

options.A: Refuse to admit any new patients until funding improves
options.B: Blame the junior nurses for failing to improvise supplies
options.C: Ignore the missing equipment and ask patients to buy everything
options.D: Maximise available resources and advocate for better supply systems

explanation: You're thinking like a true leader! A great manager makes the best of what's on hand while constantly pushing upper management for better supplies.

question: Which set of symptoms points strongly to acute chest syndrome in a hospital patient?

options.A: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.B: Yellow skin, dark urine, and severe fatigue
options.C: Chest pain, fever, and a new cough
options.D: Headache, dizziness, and sudden blurry vision

explanation: Spotting acute chest syndrome early is a key nursing skill. It acts a lot like pneumonia, showing up with chest pain, fever, and coughing because sickled cells or infections get trapped in the lungs.

question: Which action represents the correct use of alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Applying the rub and wiping the hands dry quickly with a cloth towel
options.B: Applying the rub and rubbing hands together until the solution is completely dry
options.C: Rinsing the hands with clean water right after applying the rub
options.D: Applying the rub only when wearing sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Alcohol rubs need to air-dry completely on the skin to achieve their full germ-killing effect. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why should a nurse emphasize that tubal ligation is permanent even though microsurgical reversals exist?

options.A: Reversal operations always cause permanent damage to the ovaries and uterus.
options.B: The human fallopian tubes instantly dissolve once they are surgically cut.
options.C: Reversal surgery is expensive, complex, and has uncertain success rates.
options.D: Hospitals legally forbid patients from ever attempting to reverse the procedure.

explanation: Reversing a tubal ligation requires delicate microsurgery that is not always successful, making it unwise for patients to rely on it as a backup plan. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: Who is usually the first member of the nursing team to notice small, daily changes in a resident's condition?

options.A: Director of nursing
options.B: Billing administrator
options.C: Facility pharmacist
options.D: Certified nursing assistant

explanation: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs) spend the most time with residents, making them amazing at spotting early signs of a change in health!

question: Which blood vessel carries nutrient-rich blood straight from the intestines to the liver?

options.A: Portal vein
options.B: Renal artery
options.C: Inferior vena cava
options.D: Hepatic vein

explanation: You got this! The portal vein acts like a direct highway taking blood filled with digested nutrients straight from your gut to the liver for processing.

question: When does the postpartum period officially begin?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: Twenty-four hours after delivery
options.C: When the baby takes its first breath
options.D: At the start of labor

explanation: The postnatal period kicks off right after the third stage of labor when the placenta comes out. Simple and straightforward!

question: A patient with heart failure and a leg amputation suddenly gets short of breath and has swollen ankles during therapy. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Immediate complete recovery of cardiac function
options.B: Signs of fluid overload requiring immediate evaluation
options.C: An expected side effect of occupational therapy
options.D: Normal muscle growth from the therapy session

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Sudden swelling and shortness of breath in a heart failure patient are classic red flags for fluid overload that need quick assessment.

question: A patient comes in with a metal flake stuck on the surface of their eye. Why is irrigation a good choice here?

options.A: Fluid pressure forces the metal deeper to hide the pain
options.B: Washing the eye replaces the need for a physical eye exam
options.C: Irrigation completely dissolves metal on contact
options.D: The fluid stream can safely flush away loose surface irritants

explanation: Spot on! If something is just resting loosely on the surface, a gentle, steady flow of liquid is a safe way to float it right out.

question: What special connections link heart muscle cells together so they can beat in a coordinated rhythm?

options.A: Neuromuscular junctions
options.B: Sarcoplasmic reticula
options.C: Intercalated discs
options.D: Gap-free desmosomes

explanation: Intercalated discs act like special communication highways between heart cells, letting electrical signals pass instantly so the heart pumps as one team!

question: Why is infection control still necessary in a quarantine zone where people are initially well?

options.A: To replace the need for daily temperature checks
options.B: To eliminate all bacteria from the human body permanently
options.C: To ensure that health workers do not need to wear masks
options.D: To prevent healthy residents from catching the infection from each other

explanation: If one person in quarantine is incubating the virus, poor hygiene can easily spread it to others in the same facility. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: What does the skin usually look like right after a long-term cast is removed?

options.A: Bright red, inflamed, and completely covered in blisters
options.B: Dry, scaly, and pale with accumulated dead skin cells
options.C: Deeply tanned from being shielded from outdoor sunlight
options.D: Oily, moist, and smelling strongly of fresh antiseptic lotion

explanation: Because dead skin cells couldn't shed normally while trapped in the cast, the skin looks dry and flaky when the cast finally comes off.

question: Why is it important to include the family when creating a patient's care plan?

options.A: It legally forces the family to pay all hospital bills
options.B: It ensures the plan fits their routine and improves cooperation
options.C: It stops the doctor from making any changes to the treatment
options.D: It reduces the total number of nursing shifts required

explanation: When families help build the plan, they understand it better and are much more likely to help carry it out at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which part of the male urethra is the widest and passes straight through the prostate gland?

options.A: Preprostatic segment
options.B: Spongy segment
options.C: Prostatic segment
options.D: Membranous segment

explanation: Well done! The prostatic urethra gets its name because it is snugly encased by the prostate gland.

question: Why do you still need to wash your hands right after taking off disposable gloves?

options.A: Sweat trapped inside the gloves creates a barrier that requires washing
options.B: Hospital policy requires hand washing only when gloves are completely absent
options.C: Soap activates the residual chemical powder left inside the glove material
options.D: Gloves can have tiny invisible holes or tears that allow germs through

explanation: Exactly! Gloves aren't foolproof, and microscopic tears happen. Plus, your hands can easily pick up germs while taking the gloves off. Always sanitize after!

question: When is a strong purgative commonly used in a clinical setting?

options.A: Replacing lost electrolytes after severe dehydration
options.B: Clearing the bowel before a colonoscopy or surgery
options.C: Lowering high fever during a malaria infection
options.D: Treating severe bacterial infections in the bloodstream

explanation: You're doing great! Strong purgatives are standard practice for cleaning out the intestinal tract before medical scopes or operations.

question: What is the main job of a Visiting Nurse Association (VNA) in a community?

options.A: Inspecting local restaurants for safety violations
options.B: Providing skilled nursing care and health education
options.C: Operating large regional acute care hospitals
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for home use

explanation: VNAs are set up specifically to send nurses out to homes, delivering expert nursing care and teaching families how to stay healthy.

question: What is the main reason nurses use a partograph during labor?

options.A: To screen for sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To monitor labor progress and detect deviations from normal labor early
options.C: To calculate the exact date of conception
options.D: To test the mother's blood glucose levels

explanation: You'll be seeing a lot of the partograph in the maternity ward! It's our trusty visual chart to track how labor is going and catch any warning signs early.

question: Which clinical sign tells you that an antibiotic is successfully beating the infection?

options.A: Elevation in patient blood pressure readings
options.B: Complete disappearance of normal skin flora
options.C: Increase in patient appetite within one hour
options.D: Reduction in fever and white blood cell count

explanation: Brilliant! Watching the fever drop and WBC count return to normal is a classic nursing win.

question: Which antiseptic is most commonly used to clean the skin before putting in a cannula?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Plain tap water
options.C: Chlorhexidine
options.D: Sterile mineral oil

explanation: Chlorhexidine is our go-to skin cleaner for stopping germs and keeping nasty bloodstream infections away.

question: Why does infection inside a bone cause tissue death much faster than infections in soft tissue?

options.A: Bone is trapped inside a rigid structure where swelling cuts off its blood supply
options.B: The periosteum actively feeds the bacteria instead of protecting the bone
options.C: Bones lack white blood cells entirely to fight off invading bacteria
options.D: Microorganisms multiply twice as fast inside hard calcium deposits

explanation: Because bone cannot expand, swelling and pus create high pressure inside the rigid bone cavity, which compresses blood vessels and starves the tissue of oxygen. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the main goal of emergency triage in the hospital?

options.A: To collect payment information from patients
options.B: To complete a detailed family medical history
options.C: To assign a private room to every arriving patient
options.D: To sort patients based on the severity of their condition

explanation: Great thinking! Triage is simply sorting patients by how sick they are, making sure the most critical, life-threatening cases get seen first.

question: What is your main nursing duty when giving drugs to stop excessive bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large amounts of oral rehydration fluids
options.B: Watch for the womb to contract and bleeding to slow down
options.C: Check her skin for rashes every five minutes
options.D: Keep the patient flat with her legs raised high

explanation: These drugs work by making the womb muscle squeeze tight, closing off those bleeding vessels. You're doing great with your medication checks!

question: You need to run 1000 mL of normal saline over 8 hours using a manual gravity tubing set with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What is the approximate flow rate in drops per minute?

options.A: 31 gtt/min
options.B: 125 gtt/min
options.C: 21 gtt/min
options.D: 42 gtt/min

explanation: You're doing great with math! Multiply 1000 mL by 15 to get 15,000 drops, then divide by 480 total minutes (8 hours x 60 mins). That gives you roughly 31 drops per minute!

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy in certain cancers?

options.A: To permanently increase the patient's natural testosterone and estrogen levels
options.B: To block or lower hormone levels that stimulate the growth of hormone-sensitive tumors
options.C: To completely replace failing endocrine glands throughout the entire body
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of red blood cells to prevent severe anemia

explanation: Exactly! Some cancers love hormones to grow. Hormone therapy cuts off that fuel supply to slow them down.

question: Back in the Middle Ages, who mainly cared for and sheltered the sick?

options.A: Religious orders and monasteries
options.B: Government ministries of health
options.C: Modern university medical schools
options.D: Private health insurance companies

explanation: Monks and nuns played a huge role early on, setting up early sanctuaries to offer food, shelter, and basic care.

question: Steroid hormones are primarily made from which building block?

options.A: Fatty acid chains
options.B: Cholesterol
options.C: Glucose molecules
options.D: Amino acids

explanation: Steroid hormones are lipids built from cholesterol! This fat-friendly makeup is actually what helps them easily slip right across cell membranes.

question: A patient with locked-in syndrome can't speak or move, but blinks to answer questions. What is the most important first nursing action?

options.A: Assume the patient cannot understand instructions given in the room.
options.B: Establish a reliable communication system using eye movements.
options.C: Limit neurological checks to once every twenty-four hours.
options.D: Administer heavy sedation to reduce patient awareness.

explanation: Even though they can't speak, these patients are fully conscious! Setting up a simple blink-for-yes system brings them immense comfort and dignity.

question: Where does fertilization usually happen in the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Cervical canal
options.B: Ampulla of the uterine tube
options.C: Body of the uterus
options.D: Peritoneal cavity

explanation: Spot on! Fertilization almost always takes place in the wider, middle part of the Fallopian tube (the ampulla) before the fertilized egg travels down to settle in the uterus. You've got this!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical emotional challenge faced by women with a VVF?

options.A: Severe social isolation from family and community
options.B: Anxiety about whether the surgical repair will succeed
options.C: Deep depression and profound loss of self-esteem
options.D: Feelings of complete invincibility and overconfidence

explanation: Correct! VVF patients deal with heavy emotional stress, stigma, and depression—definitely not overconfidence. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: What happens when government ministries work completely in isolation on health issues?

options.A: Community members take over all administrative responsibilities
options.B: Health workers receive higher salaries from the finance department
options.C: Opportunities to address the root causes of disease through shared resources are lost
options.D: The need for primary health care centers is completely eliminated

explanation: Spot on! When agencies refuse to cooperate, we miss out on team solutions for things like clean water, sanitation, and education.

question: How do nurses accurately measure fluid output from a heavy surgical dressing or pad?

options.A: Estimating the stain size using a common ruler
options.B: Squeezing the fluid out into a measuring cup
options.C: Asking the patient how much fluid they think leaked
options.D: Weighing the wet item and subtracting the dry weight

explanation: Weight is the most reliable way to quantify fluid soaked into solid materials, where one gram roughly equals one milliliter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when managing a sudden laryngospasm?

options.A: Calling for immediate medical assistance and emergency help
options.B: Applying 100% oxygen via a face mask or bag-valve-mask
options.C: Administering a large volume of ice-cold water by mouth
options.D: Ensuring the patient's airway remains open and unobstructed

explanation: You nailed it! Never give water by mouth when someone is having an airway spasm or can't swallow properly—that's a major choking hazard.

question: Where is compact bone primarily found in the human skeleton?

options.A: The outer shell of bones
options.B: The inner core of short bones
options.C: The center of the marrow cavity
options.D: The tips of growing joints

explanation: Spot on! Compact bone forms the tough, solid outer shell of your bones. It acts like heavy armor, protecting the inner parts and giving your body the strength to stand and move.

question: Why is it helpful to raise the head of the bed slightly when sliding a bedpan under a patient?

options.A: It stops bad room odors
options.B: It keeps the bedpan from slipping
options.C: It mimics a natural sitting posture
options.D: It stops them from falling asleep

explanation: You're right! Gravity is our friend—a slight lift helps the patient pass waste naturally and comfortably.

question: What is an important immediate action a nurse should offer after a patient passes away?

options.A: Strong sedative medications for all family members
options.B: Unhurried time for the family to sit with the body
options.C: A detailed lecture on the stages of grief
options.D: Immediate removal of the body to the morgue

explanation: Giving families peaceful, unhurried time with their loved one is a crucial first step in saying goodbye.

question: What is the main goal of reproductive coercion in a relationship?

options.A: Promoting healthy spacing between all children in a community
options.B: Ensuring family planning clinics are adequately funded
options.C: Reducing overall maternal mortality rates in rural hospitals
options.D: Controlling a partner's reproductive outcomes to maintain power

explanation: Well done! Reproductive coercion involves tactics like tampering with birth control to force or block a pregnancy, keeping the victim trapped and dependent.

question: A critically ill patient on oxygen support needs to be transferred to the CT scan room. Who is best suited to accompany this patient?

options.A: A qualified nurse or doctor with portable oxygen and emergency gear
options.B: An administrative clerk who knows the shortcut hallways well
options.C: The patient's visiting relative who agreed to watch the monitor
options.D: A hospital security guard who can help push the wheeled trolley

explanation: Unstable or critically ill patients must always be escorted by trained clinical staff equipped to handle sudden emergencies during transit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is a standard serving size for dried fruit much smaller than fresh fruit?

options.A: Dried fruit expands rapidly inside the human stomach
options.B: Manufacturers add synthetic preservatives to dried fruits
options.C: Water removal concentrates its natural sugars and calories
options.D: The digestive system cannot process dried fruit easily

explanation: That's right! Without water taking up space, dried fruit is packed tightly with natural sugars, so a smaller handful is plenty.

question: What is the primary function of a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: To record electrical impulses passing through the heart muscle
options.C: To check how well the kidneys filter waste products from urine
options.D: To detect the genetic material of a virus or bacterium

explanation: PCR tests amplify small amounts of DNA or RNA to confirm the exact presence of the infectious agent. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to approach a community health program against FGM?

options.A: Avoid discussing the topic to prevent offending local traditions
options.B: Distribute dense medical research journals to every household
options.C: Scold village elders publicly for practicing barbaric customs
options.D: Explain physiological harms respectfully while engaging community leaders

explanation: Well done! Effective prevention relies on respectful, open dialogue that partners with local influencers.

question: In the pain assessment mnemonic OPQRSTUV, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

options.A: Quantity
options.B: Quickness
options.C: Quietness
options.D: Quality

explanation: The letter Q refers to quality, prompting the nurse to ask what the pain actually feels like to the patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h3)

question: A primary nurse notices a prescribed drug dose does not match a patient's failing kidneys. What is the best action?

options.A: Wait until the next shift change to let the incoming nurse deal with it.
options.B: Advocate for the patient by contacting the physician to question the safe dosage.
options.C: Administer the medication anyway since the doctor prescribed it.
options.D: Stop all nursing documentation for the day to avoid liability.

explanation: You are the patient's safety net! Always speak up and check with the doctor if a medication dose looks unsafe for your patient's lab results.

question: How does putting a heating pad on the lower belly help with post-abortion cramps?

options.A: It stops all vaginal bleeding instantly
options.B: It numbs the skin nerves permanently
options.C: It relaxes the uterine and pelvic muscles
options.D: It lowers the body temperature safely

explanation: Warmth boosts blood flow and helps tense muscles unwind, taking the sharp edge off those cramps. Simple and effective nursing comfort care!

question: Which common condition involves the weakening of bone due to rapid mineral loss from the spongy trabeculae?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoarthritis
options.D: Osteosarcoma

explanation: You've got this! Osteoporosis means 'porous bones.' It happens when bones lose minerals too quickly, making the tiny spongy struts thin out and break easily.

question: Which of these is a typical feature of a benign (non-cancerous) tumor?

options.A: Surrounded by a fibrous capsule
options.B: Infiltrates surrounding normal tissues
options.C: Rapid and uncontrolled cellular division
options.D: Ability to form secondary tumors

explanation: Correct! Benign tumors usually stay put inside a neat fibrous capsule, meaning they don't invade nearby tissues or spread around.

question: Why is treating only the physical bleeding considered incomplete post-abortion care?

options.A: Because patients also need family planning, counseling, and ongoing support
options.B: Because patients refuse discharge until their emotional state is documented
options.C: Because physical bleeding never stops without heavy antibiotic therapy
options.D: Because surgical evacuation alone is illegal in most public hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Comprehensive PAC looks beyond the immediate medical emergency to include emotional support and future contraceptive services to prevent repeat events.

question: A resident says they feel unsteady walking to the dining hall. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Assess their footwear, use of assistive devices, and recent medications
options.B: Scold the resident for walking without supervision
options.C: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.D: Advise the resident to stay permanently in bed for safety

explanation: Finding the exact cause—like bad shoes, a missing walking stick, or a dizzying drug side effect—helps fix the problem at the root. Spot on!

question: What is a simple, free way that nurse leaders can boost daily morale on the ward?

options.A: Threatening disciplinary action for minor errors
options.B: Recognizing and acknowledging a job well done
options.C: Ignoring daily shift complaints to save time
options.D: Mandating extra weekend shifts without overtime

explanation: A simple 'Thank you, you handled that emergency brilliantly!' goes a very long way in making a nurse feel valued.

question: Why do doctors routinely order blood sugar and electrolyte tests for a patient who just had a first-time seizure?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact blood type for emergency transfusion
options.B: To measure the exact number of brain cells currently functioning
options.C: To check for fixable triggers like low sodium or low sugar
options.D: To measure the electrical resistance of the skin during muscle spasms

explanation: Spot on! Always look for reversible causes—fixing a simple electrolyte imbalance can stop further seizures.

question: Why is Crew Resource Management (CRM) so helpful for flight nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need for medical equipment maintenance
options.B: It empowers any crew member to speak up about safety hazards
options.C: It ensures pilots make all medical decisions alone
options.D: It dictates the exact medications nurses can give in flight

explanation: Brilliant! CRM makes sure that titles don't block safety. If a nurse or paramedic spots a hazard, they can speak up immediately without fear.

question: Why might some patients with cervical irritation feel absolutely no symptoms at all?

options.A: The inflammatory process can remain mild and localized without triggering pain receptors.
options.B: Hormones in the vagina completely block any physical sensation of swelling.
options.C: The body instantly neutralizes all bacterial toxins before they reach the surface.
options.D: Nerve endings in the cervix are purely motor and never transmit sensory signals.

explanation: Exactly! Mild inflammation often stays quiet without setting off pain signals, which is why regular screening tests are so important for women's health.

question: Which animal is the main definitive host for the Echinococcus tapeworm?

options.A: Human
options.B: Dog
options.C: Sheep
options.D: Cow

explanation: Dogs and other carnivores carry the adult tapeworm in their guts and pass out the eggs in their stool.

question: What is the main purpose of epidemiological surveillance in public health?

options.A: Punishing healthcare facilities that fail to report sick patients
options.B: Providing free prescription medications to rural communities
options.C: Conducting laboratory research on new pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Continuous collection and analysis of health data to guide action

explanation: Great job! Surveillance simply means keeping a close, ongoing eye on disease numbers so health workers can spot trouble early and act fast.

question: Why does the body use reflex actions?

options.A: To store long-term memories in the spinal cord
options.B: To protect the body from sudden harm without conscious thought
options.C: To consciously coordinate complex body movements
options.D: To help the brain learn new voluntary motor skills

explanation: Think of a reflex as your body's built-in alarm system! It reacts instantly to danger—like pulling your hand away from a hot stove—before your brain even has time to register the pain.

question: How does the 'collaborating' style work in the Thomas-Kilmann model?

options.A: It gives up complete control just to keep the peace on the ward.
options.B: It prioritizes personal victory over the needs of everyone else involved.
options.C: It uses low assertiveness and low cooperativeness to ignore the problem entirely.
options.D: It combines high assertiveness with high cooperativeness to find a win-win solution.

explanation: Collaboration is all about working together closely so both sides feel fully heard and completely satisfied with the result.

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of ongoing training programs for injection safety?

options.A: Reinforcing standard precautions and proper sharp disposal methods
options.B: Keeping practicing nurses updated on new safety-engineered devices
options.C: Eliminating all clinical documentation requirements for nurses
options.D: Promoting a culture of shared responsibility for health worker safety

explanation: Continuous learning helps keep our skills sharp and our wards safe, but documentation remains a vital part of professional nursing practice!

question: As a community health nurse, you notice many toddlers are malnourished in a farming village. Which non-medical sector should you involve first?

options.A: Agriculture
options.B: Judiciary
options.C: Telecommunications
options.D: Transportation

explanation: Well done! Agriculture deals with food production and farming, making them our key partner in beating chronic malnutrition at its root.

question: Which patient position is standard for examining a vulval cyst?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Lithotomy position
options.C: High Fowler position
options.D: Prone position

explanation: The lithotomy position (lying on the back with legs raised in stirrups) gives the best view and access for examining the external female genitalia safely.

question: What is the main reason a nurse gives an intradermal injection (just under the top layer of skin)?

options.A: Delivering rapid pain relief during acute trauma.
options.B: Providing daily maintenance doses of intravenous fluids.
options.C: Vaccinating large populations against seasonal influenza.
options.D: Diagnostic testing like allergy or tuberculosis screenings.

explanation: Spot on! Because skin layers absorb very slowly here, it's the perfect spot to watch for a localized immune reaction like a TB test.

question: How do poverty and transport delays worsen severe maternal illness in local communities?

options.A: They stop the fetus from growing properly inside the amniotic sac
options.B: They directly cause the placenta to detach prematurely from the uterine wall
options.C: They lower the normal blood pressure of the mother below safe levels
options.D: They prevent timely access to skilled medical care during emergencies

explanation: When transport is hard to find or money is tight, simple delays can turn a manageable emergency into a life-threatening situation. This is a huge focus in community health nursing!

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical goal of psychosocial support in hospice care?

options.A: Providing a safe space for emotional expression
options.B: Honoring the patient's personal faith and spiritual traditions
options.C: Helping the patient resolve all past family conflicts instantly
options.D: Supporting family members through anticipatory grief

explanation: While nurses support emotional processing, resolving lifelong family conflicts is rarely guaranteed or realistic in a short time frame. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h6)

question: What is the most important discharge instruction for a patient recovering from an abdominal hysterectomy?

options.A: Stop taking all prescribed pain medications immediately
options.B: Resume high-impact aerobic exercise by tomorrow
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for several weeks
options.D: Apply heat packs to the abdomen continuously every day

explanation: You nailed it! Resting and avoiding heavy loads protects the stitches and helps the belly heal properly inside.

question: Why should healthcare workers partner with traditional birth attendants (TBAs) instead of chasing them away?

options.A: To replace trained midwives with TBAs
options.B: To encourage them to refer pregnant women to clinics for skilled care
options.C: To let them manage severe bleeding at home
options.D: To train them to perform major village surgeries

explanation: Well reasoned! Since many rural women trust TBAs, working with them helps bridge the gap and guides mothers safely to professional clinic care.

question: Why would a nurse need to provide alternative ways for a patient to pass urine or stool?

options.A: The patient is unable to walk to the toilet independently
options.B: The hospital policy requires all bedridden patients to use bedpans
options.C: It reduces the total amount of daily nursing documentation
options.D: It completely prevents any risk of a hospital-acquired infection

explanation: You've got this! We bring in things like bedpans or urinals mainly when a patient is too weak or restricted to safely make it to the bathroom on their own. Simple and practical!

question: What can happen if a patient suddenly stops taking their anti-seizure medication?

options.A: It causes severe allergic skin reactions
options.B: It has no effect as long as the patient eats well
options.C: It can trigger dangerous rebound seizures or status epilepticus
options.D: It will immediately cause permanent memory loss

explanation: Abruptly quitting these drugs takes away the brain's chemical shield. It can easily lead to a scary rebound attack or even a medical emergency. Always educate patients to taper off only under doctor's orders!

question: Why do nurses use continuous IV infusions for certain medications?

options.A: Elimination of all infection risks
options.B: Exact control over blood levels
options.C: Lower cost than oral tablets
options.D: Zero requirement for site monitoring

explanation: Think of a continuous infusion as a steady drip that keeps the medicine level just right in the body over time, avoiding sudden spikes or drops.

question: What is the main reason for doing passive range of motion exercises on a bedbound patient?

options.A: To directly build large muscle mass in the limbs
options.B: To prevent joint contractures and maintain flexibility
options.C: To cure underlying systemic cardiovascular disease
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future physical therapy

explanation: You've got this! Moving joints gently keeps them from getting stiff and locked up when patients can't move themselves.

question: Why is sodium restriction a critical part of dietary education for a patient with heart failure?

options.A: Salt makes the body hold onto extra water, increasing fluid overload
options.B: Sodium prevents blood pressure medications from working properly
options.C: High sodium levels directly damage the inner lining of heart valves
options.D: Salt causes sudden blockages in the main coronary arteries

explanation: Sodium causes water retention. When a weak heart cannot pump efficiently, this extra fluid leads to dangerous swelling, shortness of breath, and worsened heart failure. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which common local Nigerian vegetable is packed with iron, calcium, and vitamins for nursing mums?

options.A: Dried white table salt
options.B: Polished white rice
options.C: Fluted pumpkin leaves (ugu)
options.D: Refined wheat flour

explanation: Dark leafy greens like ugu are local nutrition powerhouses! They are packed with the iron and vitamins needed to recover well and boost milk production.

question: What is a common mistake that can make small changes on a line graph look way bigger than they actually are?

options.A: Starting the vertical axis at a number other than zero without a break symbol
options.B: Placing the time variable on the horizontal axis
options.C: Including a clear legend for multiple lines
options.D: Using a straight ruler to connect the individual data points

explanation: You got it! Messing with the bottom of the vertical axis stretches the slope and can trick the eye into seeing a crisis where there isn't one.

question: How does poor nutrition directly weaken a patient's immune defenses?

options.A: It causes the heart to pump too slowly to circulate blood cells.
options.B: It reduces the body's ability to produce white blood cells and antibodies.
options.C: It makes the skin too thick for immune cells to travel through.
options.D: It stops the kidneys from filtering waste products out of blood.

explanation: Adequate protein and micronutrients are necessary to build immune cells and antibodies; lacking them leaves the body defenseless. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h5)

question: During which stage of Alzheimer's disease do patients typically begin to wander and experience significant personality changes?

options.A: Preclinical stage
options.B: Early stage
options.C: Terminal stage
options.D: Middle stage

explanation: The middle stage of Alzheimer's is usually the longest and brings pronounced confusion, behavioral changes like wandering, and a need for help with daily tasks. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T2#GNS222_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient asks you (the nurse) to hang out after they leave the hospital. Why is this a bad idea?

options.A: It proves the patient is trying to manipulate hospital administration
options.B: It shows the nurse has not documented patient care properly in the chart
options.C: It violates the rule that therapeutic relationships have a defined professional end
options.D: It means the patient has completely failed to recover from their illness

explanation: Professional care must end when the patient heals. Crossing over into a personal friendship blurs professional boundaries and isn't allowed.

question: What makes a well-written nursing goal?

options.A: Focused entirely on hospital routines
options.B: Written only by the attending physician
options.C: Measurable and patient-centered
options.D: Vague and open-ended for flexibility

explanation: You got it! Goals must be clear and measurable so you can easily check if your patient is actually getting better.

question: In which position should a patient be placed during a gastric lavage to reduce safety risks?

options.A: Left lateral position with the head lowered slightly
options.B: Flat on the back with legs raised high in the air
options.C: Sitting completely upright straight in a hard chair
options.D: Right lateral position with the head elevated high

explanation: The left lateral Trendelenburg position keeps the stomach contents pooled away from the pylorus and promotes safe drainage away from the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h5)

question: How does a hospital growing much larger usually affect its organisational design?

options.A: It eliminates all need for formal chains of command
options.B: It forces the organisation to become completely boundaryless
options.C: It automatically shrinks the span of control for every worker
options.D: It tends to make the organisation more mechanistic with more rules

explanation: As a hospital grows bigger, it usually adds more departments, layers, and rules to keep things organized and under control.

question: Why is the final skin closure count so tricky if everyone is tired?

options.A: The anesthesia machine might lose electrical power
options.B: The hospital will run out of disposable suture packs
options.C: A missing item can easily be overlooked when fatigue sets in
options.D: The surgeon will finish the operation too quickly

explanation: Well reasoned! Long surgeries cause fatigue, making it extra important to stay sharp during the final count. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why should you as a nurse always ask your patients if they use traditional herbs or local remedies?

options.A: To report illegal practitioners to the local authorities
options.B: To calculate the exact economic cost of local healthcare
options.C: To prevent dangerous interactions with hospital medications
options.D: To replace all expensive hospital drugs with free herbs

explanation: Patients often mix local herbs with hospital drugs without mentioning it. Checking for this helps keep them safe from unexpected drug reactions. You're learning to think like a safe, caring nurse!

question: Why is it important for the nurse to explain the rectal procedure thoroughly before beginning?

options.A: It guarantees that the drug will bypass liver metabolism
options.B: It replaces the need for wearing clean gloves during insertion
options.C: It helps reduce patient anxiety and embarrassment
options.D: It chemically speeds up the breakdown of the suppository base

explanation: The rectal procedure is sensitive and personal; clear communication builds trust and calms the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: Why do we only use glutaraldehyde on medical equipment instead of human skin?

options.A: It turns the skin bright yellow for several weeks.
options.B: It is a high-level disinfectant that releases toxic fumes and irritates skin.
options.C: It instantly evaporates when it touches human skin.
options.D: It only works when it is mixed with hot boiling water.

explanation: That's right! Glutaraldehyde is extremely harsh and gives off strong fumes, so it belongs in soaking tanks for instruments, never on a patient's skin.

question: What is a major financial barrier for families of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory free private nursing care at home
options.B: Excessive government funding for all childhood treatments
options.C: Free international travel for medical checkups
options.D: High out-of-pocket costs for therapies and medical supplies

explanation: Most families bear the financial burden of care directly because public insurance coverage for chronic disabilities is limited. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: When is surgical intervention required for a patient experiencing a haemorrhage?

options.A: Whenever external bleeding stops on its own
options.B: As the very first step before applying direct pressure
options.C: When internal bleeding cannot be stopped by non-surgical means
options.D: Only after the patient's blood pressure returns to normal

explanation: Surgery is necessary to physically find and repair damaged internal blood vessels or organs that external pressure cannot reach. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h7)

question: You need to put an IV line on a frightened preschooler. What is the best approach?

options.A: Give a detailed medical explanation of how the needle enters the vein.
options.B: Speak at the child's eye level using simple, honest, gentle words.
options.C: Ignore the child's fears and focus only on talking to the parents.
options.D: Tell the child that the needle procedure will not hurt at all.

explanation: Wonderful! Kneeling down to their level with a kind, honest voice helps calm their fears and builds instant trust.

question: What is the main goal of antimicrobial stewardship programs in hospitals?

options.A: Lowering hospital cleaning budgets by reducing soap purchases
options.B: Optimizing the use of anti-infectives to reduce resistance and harm
options.C: Ensuring every patient receives intravenous drugs automatically
options.D: Eliminating the need for laboratory cultures completely

explanation: Antimicrobial stewardship is all about using the right drug, at the right dose, for the right time—protecting patients from side effects and stopping superbugs from forming.

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when teaching a family caregiver?

options.A: It increases the cost of home care equipment
options.B: It makes the nurse look uneducated
options.C: Medical terms are illegal to use outside of hospitals
options.D: It prevents the caregiver from understanding how to safely manage care

explanation: Wonderful! Keep it simple and clear. If they don't understand the words, they won't know how to care for their loved one safely when you leave.

question: Why must a nurse check the airway before breathing and circulation during an emergency?

options.A: A blocked airway will cause death regardless of heart function
options.B: Doctors only look at the airway during emergencies
options.C: It is a hospital rule with no medical reason
options.D: Airway assessment takes the least amount of time

explanation: Makes total sense! If air can't get through, nothing else matters because the body gets zero oxygen. Clearing the airway is always step number one.

question: A patient eats a heavy carbohydrate meal, and their blood sugar goes up. What happens next?

options.A: The pituitary gland secretes growth hormone
options.B: The pancreas secretes insulin to lower blood sugar
options.C: The parathyroid glands release parathyroid hormone
options.D: The adrenal cortex stops producing aldosterone

explanation: You see this every day! High blood sugar acts as a signal to the pancreas, telling it to release insulin to bring your glucose back to normal.

question: Why is the liver considered such a vital metabolic organ for the whole body?

options.A: It processes nutrients, filters toxins, and stores essential vitamins
options.B: It produces strong mechanical churning motions to break down fiber
options.C: It pumps oxygenated blood directly through the major heart valves
options.D: It absorbs all water from solid waste before elimination

explanation: The liver is like the body's ultimate multitasking chemical factory. It handles nutrients, cleans out toxins, and stores vitamins to keep everything running smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of using a clean delivery kit during a home birth?

options.A: To speed up the progress of the first stage of labor
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing by the birth attendant
options.C: To prevent infection for both mother and newborn
options.D: To provide entertainment for the family during labor

explanation: Simple and crucial—the kit provides clean, germ-free items to stop harmful bacteria from causing infections during and after birth.

question: Why is synovial fluid usually drawn from an inflamed joint?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic osteoarthritis
options.B: To measure the total blood volume of the patient
options.C: To inject air into the joint space for better movement
options.D: To discover the underlying cause of swelling and pain

explanation: Analyzing the aspirated fluid helps doctors identify infection, crystal diseases like gout, or inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why must you turn an unconscious patient onto their side before cleaning their mouth?

options.A: To help them wake up quicker
options.B: To stop fluids from entering the airway
options.C: To reach their back teeth easily
options.D: To help them produce more saliva

explanation: You got it! A side-lying position lets water and spit flow safely out of the mouth instead of choking the patient.

question: Why must you, as the nurse, use great care when collecting laboratory specimens?

options.A: It decreases the overall cost of running hospital diagnostic equipment
options.B: It ensures the lab results reflect the true condition of the patient
options.C: It shortens the length of time the patient stays in the hospital
options.D: It removes the need for doctors to physically examine the patient

explanation: Spot-on! Good collection habits prevent errors and contamination, meaning the doctor gets accurate results to treat your patient properly.

question: Why must insulin be given as an injection instead of swallowing it as a pill?

options.A: Injections allow insulin to bypass the liver entirely
options.B: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the insulin molecule
options.C: Stomach acid turns insulin into a toxic compound
options.D: Oral pills are absorbed too rapidly to be safe

explanation: Exactly! Insulin is a protein, so the acids and enzymes in your gut would break it down before it ever reached your bloodstream if you swallowed it.

question: Why are nurses often considered the central hub of the healthcare team?

options.A: They spend the most continuous time at the patient bedside
options.B: They make all the final diagnoses for hospital admissions
options.C: They hold the legal authority to hire and fire doctors
options.D: They control the entire hospital financial budget

explanation: That's right! Because nurses are right there by the bedside around the clock, we are usually the first to notice changes and connect all the other team members.

question: Which head measurement presents when the baby's head is tilted all the way back in a brow presentation, making delivery very difficult?

options.A: Suboccipitobregmatic diameter
options.B: Occipitofrontal diameter
options.C: Biparietal diameter
options.D: Mentovertical diameter

explanation: Spot on! At 13.5 cm, the mentovertical diameter is the widest one, and it's usually too big to easily pass through an average pelvis.

question: What is the main target tissue of the somatic nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine glands
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle
options.D: Cardiac muscle

explanation: Correct! The somatic system controls your voluntary movements by talking directly to your skeletal muscles.

question: How does the body normally keep its hormone levels balanced and in check?

options.A: Negative feedback loops
options.B: Enzyme degradation
options.C: Positive feedback loops
options.D: Direct neural stimulation

explanation: Think of negative feedback as the body's natural thermostat or brake system. When hormone levels get too high, it signals the body to slow down production so everything stays balanced. You've got this!

question: Why is a severe bleeding disorder a major concern before arthrocentesis?

options.A: It completely prevents the lab from analyzing the sample
options.B: It can cause dangerous bleeding inside the joint space
options.C: It stops the local anesthetic from numbing the skin
options.D: It makes the synovial fluid too thick to withdraw

explanation: Poor clotting function puts the patient at risk of bleeding into the closed joint cavity, leading to painful hemarthrosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h3)

question: Through which structure must a flatus tube pass to enter the rectum?

options.A: The anal sphincters
options.B: The pyloric sphincter
options.C: The duodenal ampulla
options.D: The ileocecal valve

explanation: To enter the rectum safely, the tube needs to pass through the internal and external anal sphincters. You've got this!

question: What specific characteristic of a skin test reaction must the nurse measure?

options.A: Induration
options.B: Erythema
options.C: Bruising
options.D: Warmth

explanation: Induration refers to the hard, raised swelling caused by cellular immune activity, which is the true indicator of a positive test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: Who is a key partner in sustaining school health initiatives within the local area?

options.A: Commercial advertising agencies
options.B: Foreign manufacturing industries
options.C: International sports federations only
options.D: The Parent-Teacher Association (PTA)

explanation: PTAs connect the school with parents and community members who provide vital support and resources for health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: What does 'therapeutic use of self' mean in nursing?

options.A: Using your personality and insights to connect with patients
options.B: Hiding all personal feelings behind a cold professional mask
options.C: Acting as a close personal friend outside of work hours
options.D: Sharing your own personal medical history with every patient

explanation: Spot on! It means using your own communication style and warmth on purpose to build trust and help the patient feel safe.

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?

options.A: Immediate government employment
options.B: Automatic university admission
options.C: Lifelong economic hardship
options.D: Complete immunity from malaria

explanation: Interrupting education early often limits future career opportunities, leading to long-term financial struggles. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: What is the clinical benefit of providing a wide variety of choices in family planning services?

options.A: The clinic can avoid stocking pills and focus only on injectables
options.B: It eliminates all possible side effects associated with hormones
options.C: Clients can choose contraception that fits their personal lifestyle and health needs
options.D: Nurses can force every client to use long-acting contraceptives

explanation: Brilliant! Giving clients options respects their autonomy and helps them find a method that genuinely matches their lifestyle and health profile.

question: Why must you be careful of the chemical reaction when mixing Plaster of Paris with water?

options.A: It generates heat as it sets and hardens
options.B: It produces toxic fumes during mixing
options.C: It expands to double its original size
options.D: It absorbs ambient room moisture rapidly

explanation: The setting process is exothermic, meaning it gives off heat. You want to keep this in mind so it doesn't cause skin discomfort or burns!

question: What is obstetric fistula?

options.A: The premature closing of the birth canal due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: A sudden infection of the outer reproductive organs during early pregnancy
options.C: An abnormal opening between the vagina and bladder or rectum caused by prolonged labor
options.D: A complete failure of the ovaries to release eggs during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Well done! When labor is blocked in a narrow pelvis, the crushed tissue dies, leaving a hole (fistula) that causes leaking of urine or stool. It's a devastating condition we work hard to prevent.

question: Which dangerous electrolyte imbalance is most life-threatening in advanced kidney failure?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Hypocalcemia
options.C: Hypermagnesemia
options.D: Hyperkalemia

explanation: High potassium (hyperkalemia) is a major emergency because it messes with the heart's electrical rhythm and can lead to sudden cardiac arrest if not treated quickly.

question: How do soaps and surfactants mainly destroy germs on the skin?

options.A: By freezing the internal water inside the cell
options.B: By blocking the cell from taking in sunlight
options.C: By turning the cell into pure oxygen gas
options.D: By disrupting and breaking down the outer cell membrane

explanation: Exactly! Surfactants attack the fatty outer layer of the germ's cell wall, causing it to burst open and spill its contents.

question: Which heart rhythm do adults in sudden cardiac arrest show most often?

options.A: Atrial flutter
options.B: First-degree heart block
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: In ventricular fibrillation, the lower chambers just quiver uselessly instead of pumping. Recognizing this rhythm is a key nursing skill!

question: Which mineral salt makes up the hard inorganic part of bone matrix?

options.A: Sodium chloride
options.B: Potassium sulfate
options.C: Calcium phosphate
options.D: Magnesium carbonate

explanation: Calcium phosphate crystals combine with other minerals to form hydroxyapatite, giving bone its hard, rigid quality. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of these should you NOT do when teaching a community during an outbreak?

options.A: Using complex medical jargon to show professional superiority
options.B: Listening carefully to community fears and answering questions
options.C: Explaining simple preventive habits like handwashing clearly
options.D: Collaborating directly with respected local and religious leaders

explanation: Never use heavy grammar or jargon to intimidate patients! Always keep your health education simple, respectful, and easy to grasp.

question: Why is it so important to send a routine urine sample to the lab right away, or keep it in the fridge if there's a delay?

options.A: Prompt delivery prevents the patient from changing their mind about the test
options.B: Room temperature encourages bacterial growth and chemical breakdown
options.C: Leaving it out causes the plastic container to melt in warm rooms
options.D: Refrigeration speeds up the chemical reaction on dipstick pads

explanation: Urine left sitting in a warm room changes quickly—bacteria love to multiply in it, and cellular casts start to break apart, which ruins the accuracy of the test!

question: Why is nursing care for inherited degenerative disorders focused on comfort rather than a cure?

options.A: Medications can completely reverse the genetic mutation if given early.
options.B: Hospital policies restrict long-term curative therapies for chronic illnesses.
options.C: The underlying genetic damage causes progressive and irreversible cell death.
options.D: Clients usually recover spontaneously once they reach middle age.

explanation: Because these conditions involve continuous cellular breakdown from genetics, treatment focuses on managing symptoms and keeping the patient as comfortable as possible.

question: Which adaptive tool helps a patient with shaky hands eat on their own?

options.A: A long-handled reacher
options.B: Weighted utensils
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A rigid gait belt

explanation: You got it! Heavy spoons and forks help steady shaky hands so food actually makes it to the mouth.

question: When you are taking a nursing history from a patient, what kind of information are you mainly collecting?

options.A: Subjective data from the patient
options.B: Objective data from laboratory tests
options.C: Biochemical data from blood samples
options.D: Radiological data from imaging scans

explanation: You've got this! History taking is all about listening to what the patient tells you about how they feel. That direct information is called subjective data.

question: What usually causes a 'Check Pads' error message to pop up on a defibrillator screen?

options.A: Poor skin contact or loose cable connections
options.B: The patient has an implanted cardiac pacemaker
options.C: The room oxygen level is dangerously high
options.D: The battery is completely charged to maximum capacity

explanation: A 'Check Pads' warning simply means the machine isn't sensing a clean electrical connection with the skin. Check your leads and pad placement!

question: Why do doctors prescribe multiple antibiotics at once to treat an H. pylori infection?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing common side effects
options.B: To speed up the healing time of the skin across the abdomen
options.C: To prevent the bacterium from developing resistance to single drug therapies
options.D: To replace the intrinsic factor lost during chronic inflammation

explanation: You got it! H. pylori is tough, so combining drugs stops the bacteria from outsmarting a single antibiotic and clears the infection completely.

question: Why do people often get confused by the word 'stress' in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: They believe it is caused by mental exhaustion
options.B: They assume it only happens during high-intensity sports
options.C: They confuse it with neurological distress
options.D: They think it relates to emotional anxiety rather than physical pressure

explanation: It's an easy mix-up! In this case, 'stress' means physical force or pressure on your organs, not emotional stress or worry.

question: What do we call someone who carries and spreads a germ without looking or feeling sick?

options.A: A primary reservoir
options.B: An indirect vector
options.C: An asymptomatic carrier
options.D: A susceptible host

explanation: Correct! Asymptomatic carriers harbor and spread germs while feeling completely healthy themselves. That's why universal precautions matter so much!

question: What is the main difference between the ureters and the urethra?

options.A: Ureters store urine, while the urethra filters waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: Ureters and urethra perform the exact same task on opposite sides of the pelvis
options.C: Ureters carry urine from kidneys to the bladder, while the urethra carries urine outside the body
options.D: Ureters pump urine out of the body, while the urethra connects the kidneys directly to the outside

explanation: Think of ureters as the pipes coming down from the kidneys to the bladder, and the urethra as the final exit tube to the outside world!

question: What are those bony bumps that form on the edges of joints in osteoarthritis called?

options.A: Osteoids
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteoclasts
options.D: Osteophytes

explanation: Osteophytes are commonly known as bone spurs. They form when the bone tries to repair itself after losing smooth cartilage.

question: What is the main purpose of using a syringe driver in clinical practice?

options.A: To flush blocked intravenous lines rapidly with sterile saline
options.B: To deliver a continuous, controlled amount of medication
options.C: To provide intermittent bolus doses every five minutes
options.D: To measure precise hourly urine output in critical care

explanation: A syringe driver is specifically designed to infuse medications slowly and steadily over a set duration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is keeping things strictly confidential vital for youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Government insurance schemes refuse to pay claims if patient names are published
options.B: Traditional leaders demand exclusive rights to review all clinic patient logs
options.C: Fear of social stigma and exposure will drive young people to seek unsafe, clandestine alternatives
options.D: Hospitals lack physical filing cabinets to store confidential adolescent records

explanation: Exactly! If young people are afraid their families or communities will find out, they'll stay away from clinics and risk unsafe options. Privacy saves lives!

question: Why is vocational training an important part of holistic fistula care?

options.A: It teaches the patient how to use specialized machinery to clean hospital linen
options.B: It helps survivors regain financial independence and rebuild their lives after social stigma
options.C: It acts as a substitute for medical treatment when surgery fails to close the hole
options.D: It trains the patient to perform minor surgical repairs on other women in the village

explanation: Great job! Learning a trade empowers these women economically, helping them bounce back from poverty and isolation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why is performing last offices calmly so important for the family?

options.A: It gives grieving relatives a sense of peace and comfort
options.B: It prevents the family from asking too many questions
options.C: It speeds up the process of issuing a death certificate
options.D: It proves to the doctor that death actually occurred

explanation: Seeing a loved one cared for gently and professionally helps reassure the family that the patient was valued until the very end. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who admits to using traditional herbal remedies?

options.A: By threatening to discharge the patient immediately from the hospital
options.B: By prescribing synthetic antibiotics to replace the herbal mixture
options.C: With an open, non-judgmental attitude to encourage honest communication
options.D: By laughing at the remedies to show they have no scientific value

explanation: Keeping a welcoming, non-judgmental vibe makes patients trust us enough to share everything they're taking.

question: Why should nurses use open-ended questions when talking to a child about an injury?

options.A: To avoid leading the child and contaminating potential legal evidence
options.B: To speed up the clinical assessment process during busy shifts
options.C: To comply with hospital billing guidelines for pediatric trauma
options.D: To encourage the child to blame their siblings instead of parents

explanation: Asking leading questions puts words in the child's mouth, which ruins the reliability of any future legal investigation.

question: What essential details should you include in your nursing notes after an ear exam?

options.A: A detailed diagram of the patient's skull bones and cranial nerves
options.B: The appearance of the canal, eardrum color, landmark visibility, and any abnormal findings
options.C: The exact brand and serial number of the otoscope device used
options.D: Only the patient's reported hearing test scores from previous years

explanation: Good clinical notes always describe what you actually saw—like the color of the eardrum and whether landmarks were clear—so you can track the patient's healing.

question: Why does your nose feel so stuffy and congested when you catch a cold?

options.A: Inflammatory mediators cause local blood vessels to dilate and leak fluid into tissues
options.B: Infiltrating bacteria block the normal flow of air through the sinus passages
options.C: The nasal cartilage permanently expands in response to cold temperatures
options.D: Inhaled dust particles accumulate rapidly because cilia stop growing

explanation: When your immune system fights a cold virus, blood vessels in your nose widen and swell up, letting fluid leak into the tissues. This narrows your airway and creates that annoying stuffy feeling!

question: Why might some families try to hide harmful traditional practices from community health nurses during home visits?

options.A: Cultural laws that forbid speaking to healthcare workers in private
options.B: Ignorance regarding the exact location of the nearest health center
options.C: Belief that nurses are legally required to provide free food supplies
options.D: Fear of legal penalties or social judgment from health authorities

explanation: Because practices like child marriage or FGM are increasingly against the law, families hide them out of fear. Building trust as a nurse is the best way to gently break through this wall.

question: How do advocacy groups empower individuals who are going through rehabilitation?

options.A: By taking away their legal right to make personal decisions
options.B: By forcing them to rely exclusively on charitable handouts
options.C: By isolating them from mainstream political conversations
options.D: By giving them a collective voice to lobby for their rights

explanation: There is strength in numbers! Advocacy groups help people join together to demand better accessibility, fair treatment, and policy changes.

question: Why are direct-acting vasodilators often given along with a beta-blocker?

options.A: To stop the sudden accumulation of fluid in the lower ankles
options.B: To prevent the development of a persistent dry hacking cough
options.C: To prevent the compensatory reflex increase in heart rate
options.D: To enhance the potassium-sparing effects in the kidney tubules

explanation: Correct! The beta-blocker acts like a brake to stop the heart from racing too fast (reflex tachycardia) when the vasodilator opens up the blood vessels.

question: How can a broken receptor cause health issues even if hormone levels are completely normal?

options.A: The excess hormone begins to crystallize inside the major organs
options.B: The immune system mistakes the healthy hormone for a foreign bacteria
options.C: The liver is forced to clear all circulating hormones too quickly
options.D: The target cells fail to respond or fire signals constantly without a trigger

explanation: Picture a broken lock: either the key won't turn at all, or the latch is stuck wide open and keeps firing signals when it shouldn't. Either way, trouble follows! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h3)

question: A nurse researcher wants to understand how patients feel emotionally while recovering from open-heart surgery. Which design is most appropriate?
