options.A: Qualitative design
options.B: Laboratory chemical analysis
options.C: Quantitative experimental design
options.D: Financial audit design

explanation: Qualitative designs excel at capturing deep human experiences, feelings, and personal perspectives. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference between HIV and AIDS?

options.A: HIV only affects children whereas AIDS affects adults.
options.B: HIV is transmitted by blood while AIDS is transmitted sexually.
options.C: AIDS can be cured completely with antibiotics unlike HIV.
options.D: AIDS is the advanced stage when the immune system is severely damaged.

explanation: Think of HIV as the virus that enters the body, and AIDS as the later stage when the immune system gets very weak and can no longer fight off sickness.

question: When opening a wrapped sterile package on your tray, which flap should you open first?

options.A: The left side flap of the paper wrap
options.B: The right side flap of the paper wrap
options.C: The flap furthest away from the body
options.D: The flap closest to the nurse's chest

explanation: You've got this! Opening the far flap first means your hands won't have to reach directly across the clean items you just exposed. Smart and safe!

question: What is the main focus during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Gathering baseline lab results before surgery
options.B: Determining whether the patient has achieved the expected care goals
options.C: Writing the initial health history admission paperwork
options.D: Deciding which medication to prescribe next without a doctor

explanation: Correct! Evaluation is all about checking back: did the patient reach the goals you set together during planning?

question: Which sign points strongly to a wound infection after a skin biopsy?

options.A: A thin line of pink tissue along the suture line
options.B: Temporary numbness fading after the local anesthetic wears off
options.C: Spreading redness, warmth, and purulent drainage
options.D: Mild itching around the edges of the adhesive bandage

explanation: Redness that keeps spreading, feeling hot to the touch, pus (purulent drainage), and worsening pain are classic red flags that bacteria have moved in.

question: How can stagnant water or soil act as a source of community infection?

options.A: By attracting human carriers to contaminated areas
options.B: By turning into clinical cases of human disease
options.C: By harboring environmental bacteria and fungal spores that enter the body
options.D: By mutating human cells to create new viruses

explanation: Soil and water can hold onto tough bacteria and spores. When people come into contact with them through breaks in the skin or swallowing, an infection can start.

question: What is the most common primary bone cancer in teens and young adults?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Osteosarcoma
options.C: Chondrosarcoma
options.D: Ewing sarcoma

explanation: Osteosarcoma loves to show up during adolescent growth spurts, usually around the knee area. You've got this!

question: How often should vital signs be monitored immediately after an MVA procedure during the first hour?

options.A: Only if the patient complains of dizziness
options.B: Every hour on the hour
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Frequent checks every 15 minutes during the first hour help catch early signs of hemorrhage or vasovagal shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Why is treating the root cause the most important step when caring for a patient with DIC?

options.A: It stops the continuous, abnormal activation of the clotting cascade.
options.B: It immediately replaces all lost red blood cells and platelets.
options.C: It reverses the inherited genetic mutation causing the disease.
options.D: It prevents the patient from experiencing allergic reactions to plasma.

explanation: DIC is triggered by an underlying problem like an infection or severe injury. Until you fix that main trigger, the body will just keep overusing its clotting resources!

question: At what CD4+ cell count is an HIV infection typically classified as AIDS?

options.A: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 1000 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 1500 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 200 cells per microliter

explanation: When the CD4 count drops below 200 cells per microliter, it shows severe immune weakness and meets the clinical definition of AIDS.

question: Which landmark sits right between the front and back fontanelles on a baby's head?

options.A: The mentum
options.B: The vertex
options.C: The base
options.D: The face

explanation: You've got this! The vertex is simply the top part of the head, located right between the two main soft spots (fontanelles).

question: A researcher notices many patients stopped attending a 6-month weight loss study before it ended. What is this called?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: A confounding variable
options.C: Attrition bias
options.D: Random assignment

explanation: You nailed it! 'Attrition' just means people dropping out over time, which can leave us with a lopsided group of results.

question: Which medication is the main choice for treating onchocerciasis?

options.A: Ivermectin
options.B: Penicillin
options.C: Chloroquine
options.D: Quinine

explanation: Ivermectin is the superstar drug used worldwide to clear out microfilariae and protect people's sight.

question: What happens to a patient's blood pressure reading if you use a cuff that is too small for their arm?

options.A: The blood pressure reading will be falsely low
options.B: The mercury column will fail to rise at all
options.C: The reading will remain completely normal
options.D: The blood pressure reading will be falsely high

explanation: A tiny cuff squeezes too hard against a big arm, making the reading look much higher than it really is. Always match your cuff size to the patient!

question: What special room feature do you need for a patient on Airborne Precautions?

options.A: Negative pressure airflow
options.B: An attached private sunroom
options.C: Open windows for natural breeze
options.D: Positive pressure ventilation

explanation: A negative pressure room pulls air in instead of blowing it out into the hallway when the door opens, trapping germs inside.

question: Why is documenting vaccine administration in the child health card important?

options.A: It creates an accurate health record to guide future clinical care
options.B: It acts as a legal receipt for fees paid at the clinic counter
options.C: It proves to the government that the nurse worked a full shift
options.D: It prevents mothers from visiting any other health facility ever again

explanation: Clear documentation ensures subsequent providers know which doses were given and when the next ones are due. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: What happens when clinic staff guess tally counts on extremely busy days?

options.A: It leads to distorted health statistics that misguide national disease planning and resource allocation.
options.B: It causes client folders to physically deteriorate faster.
options.C: It automatically increases the clinic budget allocation.
options.D: It results in the immediate suspension of the senior nurse.

explanation: Guessed data leads to bad government decisions. If the numbers say you treated 50 kids for malaria when it was actually 500, the next drug supply shipment will be way too small!

question: What is the medical term for the exaggerated inward curve of the lower back seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Cervical subluxation
options.B: Compensatory lumbar lordosis
options.C: Thoracic scoliosis
options.D: Lateral kyphosis

explanation: Lordosis is just the natural inward curve of the lower back. During pregnancy, it becomes more pronounced (exaggerated) to help balance out the heavy bump.

question: Why must an adult patient fast before having an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

options.A: To make sure the patient loses weight during the hospital stay
options.B: To speed up the action of the sedative medication
options.C: To prevent the camera from heating up inside the stomach
options.D: To prevent aspiration of stomach contents into the lungs

explanation: Safety first! An empty stomach ensures the patient won't vomit and accidentally breathe food or liquid into their lungs while sedated.

question: Why do many men often spread STIs without even knowing they have them?

options.A: Male anatomy completely blocks bacterial growth
options.B: Common pathogens only survive inside female tissues
options.C: Many infected men show no early symptoms at all
options.D: Routine blood tests always cure the infection early

question: Which chronic viral infections are most commonly linked to intravenous drug use?

options.A: Malaria and Yellow Fever
options.B: HIV and Hepatitis C
options.C: Herpes and Chickenpox
options.D: Influenza and Tuberculosis

explanation: Sharing needles or injection equipment is a primary transmission route for blood-borne viruses like HIV and hepatitis C. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why is encouraging joint spousal counseling important in family planning?

options.A: It helps couples share responsibility and align their family goals
options.B: It allows the nurse to charge higher fees for the visit
options.C: It ensures that only the male partner makes the final choice
options.D: It prevents the couple from ever visiting the clinic again

explanation: Joint counseling promotes healthy communication, reducing secrets and helping partners make decisions together for their shared future. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand female reproductive anatomy?

options.A: To prescribe hormonal contraceptives without a doctor
options.B: To diagnose sexually transmitted infections by sight alone
options.C: To accurately assess health problems and provide patient care
options.D: To perform surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy helps you spot when something isn't quite right, chat easily with your patients, and guide them through different stages of life with confidence.

question: Why is regular skin monitoring necessary while a poultice is in place?

options.A: To catch early signs of thermal burns or irritation
options.B: To measure how much weight the patient gained
options.C: To see if the bandages can be sold again
options.D: To check if the patient is sleeping soundly

explanation: Frequent checks ensure that heat or active ingredients do not damage or blister the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: What term is used in Islam for foods that are unlawful or forbidden?

options.A: Haram
options.B: Treifah
options.C: Halal
options.D: Kosher

explanation: Haram simply means forbidden by Islamic law. This includes items like pork, alcohol, and meat that wasn't slaughtered according to religious rites.

question: Why is family counseling so valuable when coping with a progressive illness?

options.A: It forces family members to move into the same household
options.B: It eliminates all future disagreements about financial matters
options.C: It helps resolve conflicts and adjust roles regarding care responsibilities
options.D: It proves which family member caused the inherited genetic mutation

explanation: As illnesses progress, family roles shift. Counseling gives everyone a safe space to talk openly and share the care burden smoothly.

question: In which zone of the surgical suite are hospital staff still allowed to wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Sterile core zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the front area where you enter and receive patients before changing into your fresh theatre scrubs. Easy peasy!

question: Which public health measure helps protect people from getting human papillomavirus (HPV)?

options.A: Surgical removal
options.B: Daily antibiotics
options.C: Vaccination
options.D: Vitamin C therapy

explanation: You got it! Vaccines are our best primary defense because they train the immune system to fight off viruses like HPV before exposure ever happens.

question: What is the most reliable way to check if a patient actually has a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday
options.B: Observing the color of the patient's skin
options.C: Laboratory blood tests
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure

question: Why does a nurse ask about other body systems when a patient comes in with joint pain?

options.A: It proves that the joint pain is entirely psychological in origin
options.B: Systemic symptoms never occur alongside orthopedic complaints
options.C: It replaces the need to ask about the patient's current medications

explanation: Great job! Joint pain is often just one piece of a bigger puzzle involving the whole body, like an autoimmune condition.

question: Which clinical sign tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway blockage rather than a lower airway problem?

options.A: Expiratory wheezing
options.B: Bilateral basal crackles
options.C: Intercostal recession
options.D: Inspiratory stridor

question: What is the main job of reference apps like Zotero or Mendeley?

options.A: To write entire nursing essays and research papers
options.B: To block websites that contain plagiarized text
options.C: To store sources and automatically generate citations
options.D: To check student assignments for spelling errors only

explanation: Nice one! These tools save you stress by keeping your sources organized and generating citations for you.

question: What should the nurse do immediately if resistance is felt while advancing the flatus tube?

options.A: Inject warm tap water through the lumen
options.B: Push harder to bypass the blockage
options.C: Rotate the tube rapidly in a circle
options.D: Stop advancing and remove the tube immediately

question: How does general inflation negatively affect a Drug Revolving Fund over time?

options.A: It causes all tablets inside the store to dissolve faster
options.B: It increases the number of qualified pharmacists available
options.C: It prevents patients from visiting the hospital entirely
options.D: It reduces the purchasing power of the fund over time

explanation: When prices go up everywhere, the cash you have buys fewer replacement drugs than it used to. That's the challenge of inflation!

question: Which past medical history is most important when assessing a male patient's fertility risks?

options.A: A normal resting heart rate and blood pressure reading
options.B: A history of undescended testicles in childhood
options.C: A personal preference for wearing loose cotton clothing
options.D: Occasional mild muscle soreness after heavy exercise

question: A patient develops a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump at an injection site a few days after treatment. What is this likely a sign of?

options.A: A mild allergic reaction to clean cotton wool
options.B: An expected systemic reaction to vitamin supplements
options.C: A local bacterial infection and abscess formation
options.D: The normal healing process of deep muscle tissue

explanation: Ouch! When unsterile equipment or poor technique introduces bacteria into the tissue, it causes localized inflammation and can form a nasty abscess.

question: Why is it important for nurses to study both morbidity and mortality statistics together?

options.A: To prove that nobody gets sick in rural areas
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To see which illnesses cause suffering versus which ones cause death
options.D: To calculate the exact salary of medical doctors

explanation: Looking at both illness rates and death rates provides a complete picture of the total health burden affecting a population. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: What does hydronephrosis mean when seen on an IVP result?

options.A: An infection caused by bacteria inside the bladder wall

options.C: Bleeding originating from the inner lining of the ureters

question: In Nigeria, under what single main condition is an abortion legally allowed?

question: What is the primary purpose of control measures in drug administration?

options.A: To reduce the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily
options.B: To speed up the process of discharging patients from the ward
options.C: To protect patients from potential medication errors and harm
options.D: To help the hospital pharmacy manage its drug inventory better

explanation: Control measures exist primarily as safety barriers to prevent medication mistakes and keep patients safe from harm during treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which body language helps build instant trust during a home visit?

options.A: Standing over the patient while writing notes rapidly
options.B: Checking your wristwatch every two minutes
options.C: Crossing your arms tightly across your chest
options.D: Sitting down at eye level with open body language

question: What is the immediate priority when caring for a patient who has just suffered a severe burn injury?

options.A: Applying antibiotic ointment to all blistered areas
options.B: Calculating the total body surface area burned
options.C: Inserting a large-bore intravenous line for pain meds
options.D: Securing the airway and assessing breathing

explanation: Airway stability always comes first in trauma and burn management because smoke inhalation or laryngeal edema can quickly cause suffocation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h6)

question: Why doesn't the mother's immune system attack and reject the fetus as a foreign body?

options.A: The syncytiotrophoblast lacks the usual antigens that trigger immune rejection
options.B: Fetal blood cells destroy any maternal immune cells that enter the cord
options.C: The amniotic fluid contains strong chemicals that destroy antibodies
options.D: The mother stops producing white blood cells entirely during pregnancy

question: A patient has an issue with making and circulating cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. Which cells are directly involved?

options.A: Satellite cells
options.B: Astrocytes

options.D: Schwann cells

question: What is a common argument progressive religious leaders use to discourage FGM?

options.A: Science proves that cutting actually reduces female fertility

question: A pregnant patient comes in with a pounding headache, changes in her vision, and very high blood pressure. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Uterine atony
options.C: Placenta previa
options.D: Preeclampsia

question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of choosing whole fruit over fruit juice?

options.B: Providing a concentrated dose of liquid sugar

question: What is the primary characteristic of acute renal failure?

options.A: A gradual increase in the body's red blood cell count

options.C: A sudden and rapid decline in kidney function

question: Why must nurses in local community clinics look beyond hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Environmental and economic living conditions heavily impact health outcomes
options.B: Nurses are forbidden from providing care outside of enclosed rooms
options.C: Community members never visit hospitals for severe medical problems
options.D: Lab tests can only be accurately performed in outdoor market stalls

explanation: Understanding a patient's home and community environment helps explain why illnesses occur and how to prevent them. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why must a nurse carefully inspect the skin over a joint before an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To determine the best clothing size for the patient
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the surrounding muscle
options.C: To check if the patient has any permanent tattoos on the limb
options.D: To make sure there is no active skin infection that could spread into the joint

explanation: Injecting through broken or infected skin carries bacteria straight into the sterile joint space, causing severe infection. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of hemostasis in the human body?

options.A: To produce new red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: To pump blood efficiently through the heart
options.C: To transport oxygen and nutrients to body tissues
options.D: To stop bleeding from injured blood vessels

explanation: Hemostasis is the specific physiological response designed to halt bleeding and repair vascular injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)?

options.A: A fast and pounding heartbeat
options.B: Shaking hands and muscle tremors
options.C: Intolerance to cold temperatures
options.D: Sudden and unexplained weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! When the metabolism slows down due to low thyroid hormone, patients feel chilly even when everyone else is warm.

question: When is the best time to talk about advance directives with a patient diagnosed with a brain degenerative disease?

options.A: Family members should make all choices without consulting the patient
options.B: After the patient has completely lost the ability to speak or think
options.C: Early in the disease process while the patient can still make decisions
options.D: During an emergency room visit in the final week of life

explanation: Makes total sense! Talking early ensures the patient's own values guide their future care before cognitive decline takes away their voice. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h7)

question: What is a major public health challenge linked to teenage pregnancies?

options.A: Immediate onset of chronic hypertension
options.B: Permanent cessation of natural bone growth
options.C: Decreased overall societal life expectancy
options.D: Increased maternal morbidity and mortality

explanation: Complications from early childbirth and unsafe procedures are major reasons young mothers face serious health risks. You've got this!

question: As a nurse in an IDP camp, you notice a sudden spike in watery diarrhea among children. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Contaminated drinking water sources
options.B: A sudden increase in local mosquito populations
options.C: Genetically inherited chronic bowel disorders
options.D: Routine administration of oral polio vaccines

explanation: Waterborne outbreaks like cholera or diarrhea are usually linked to unsafe drinking water in temporary settlements.

question: What is the most important nursing duty right after a patient has a bone marrow test?

options.A: Stop them from drinking any fluids for 12 hours
options.B: Take off the pressure dressing in five minutes
options.C: Get them up to do heavy exercises
options.D: Watch the puncture site closely for bleeding

explanation: Because the needle goes right into the bone, keeping an eye on the site for bleeding or swelling is a top priority to keep your patient safe.

question: What is a big advantage of making drugs in a lab instead of harvesting plants?

options.A: It is not dependent on weather or farming seasons
options.B: It eliminates the need for any quality control testing
options.C: It guarantees that the drug will never cause side effects
options.D: It makes the medication completely free for all hospitals

explanation: Lab-made drugs mean we never have to worry about droughts, poor crop yields, or animal diseases disrupting our medicine supply.

question: A community health nurse notices a 12-year-old girl has suddenly stopped coming to school and clinic. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the absence since it falls outside routine clinical nursing duties
options.B: Investigate the reason for absence through a home visit or family talk
options.C: Report the family to the international criminal court immediately
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to see if the child returns on her own

explanation: That's right! A sudden dropout is a red flag. Checking in with the family helps you find out what's going on and offer support early.

question: What happens when a drug that slows down liver enzymes is taken with another medication?

options.A: The second drug is excreted through the kidneys within minutes
options.B: The second drug binds more tightly to plasma proteins in the blood
options.C: The second drug breaks down slower, increasing the risk of toxicity
options.D: The second drug absorbs much faster from the stomach lining

explanation: If the liver's processing speed is slowed down, the companion drug hangs around longer instead of clearing out. Over time, it builds up in the blood to levels that can become toxic.

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbal supplements when you ask about their medications?

options.A: Supplements never interact with prescription medications
options.B: Pharmacists automatically upload supplement lists to charts
options.C: Federal laws prohibit patients from discussing herbs in hospitals
options.D: They do not consider supplements to be real medicine

explanation: You got it! Because herbs and vitamins are bought over-the-counter, patients often don't think to mention them, even though they can interact with drugs.

question: How does organizing the partograph into specific sections help you as a busy nurse?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to ever take manual blood pressure
options.B: It reduces the total duration of the first stage of labour by half
options.C: It ensures systematic and organized data collection without missing vital signs
options.D: It allows family members to fill out the medical chart independently

explanation: Having dedicated sections keeps your charting neat and ensures you never forget a vital check for either the mother or her baby.

question: What exactly is a lactocele?

options.A: A milk-filled cyst formed from a blocked duct
options.B: An acute bacterial infection of the milk glands
options.C: A normal physiological swelling during milk let-down
options.D: A malignant tumor common in postpartum women

explanation: A lactocele is simply a pocket containing trapped milk that forms when a duct stays blocked. You're doing great!

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves do we have in our body?

options.A: Twenty-four pairs
options.B: Twelve pairs
options.C: Ten pairs
options.D: Thirty-one pairs

explanation: You've got this! There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves coming straight from the brain to help manage our head, neck, and organs.

question: A patient calls the clinic worried because she has heavy cramps and is passing large clots after taking misoprostol. As a nurse, how do you view this?

options.A: It means the entire treatment has completely failed.
options.B: It is the expected normal physical response to the drugs.
options.C: It indicates a dangerous uterine rupture.
options.D: It is a sign of a severe medication allergy.

explanation: Brilliant! Heavy cramping and passing clots show that the medication is working and the uterus is emptying as it should.

question: What is the everyday medical name for the outer, visible part of the ear?

options.A: Eustachian tube
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Auricle
options.D: Cochlea

explanation: Great job! The auricle (or pinna) is shaped just right to catch sounds and funnel them down into the ear canal.

question: Why do community nurses rely heavily on basic anthropometric tools like measuring tapes?

options.A: Advanced hospital equipment is always brought to the field
options.B: Blood tests are illegal outside of licensed hospitals
options.C: Patients prefer tape measurements over physical examinations
options.D: They allow quick screening of large populations in remote areas

explanation: Remote clinics lack heavy laboratory equipment, so nurses use simple tools to screen many people efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

options.A: It represents the maximum depth of permanent skin and muscle destruction.
options.B: Infection rarely occurs in this specific layer of the burn wound.
options.C: This area is completely insensate and requires immediate surgical removal.
options.D: Tissue in this zone has reduced blood flow and can be saved from necrosis.

explanation: The zone of stasis is bruised and sluggish, but not dead yet! Quick fluids keep blood flowing there so it doesn't cross over into tissue death (necrosis). Great nursing care saves the day!

question: A newly intubated patient is on a ventilator. You notice the left side of the chest is barely moving and you cannot hear breath sounds there. What likely happened?

options.A: The ventilator settings have too much positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: The tube has slipped into the right mainstem bronchus
options.C: The oxygen source has become disconnected from the machine
options.D: The patient is developing a severe tension pneumothorax

explanation: The right breathing pipe (bronchus) is a straight shot down, so tubes often slide too far in and end up ventilating only the right lung, leaving the left side quiet.

question: What does an autoclave mainly use to achieve full sterilization?

options.A: Dry scorching hot air
options.B: Toxic formaldehyde gas
options.C: Ultraviolet light rays
options.D: Moist heat under pressure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam, which packs enough heat to rapidly destroy all germs and spores.

question: Why do many men unknowingly spread STIs to their partners?

options.A: They only transmit infections during the winter months
options.B: They refuse to take oral medications prescribed by nurses
options.C: They develop immediate immunity that masks active laboratory results
options.D: They frequently harbour asymptomatic infections without realising it

explanation: Many guys walk around feeling totally fine with zero symptoms (asymptomatic), which is why testing is so important even when someone feels healthy!

question: An elevated white blood cell (WBC) count usually points to what in a patient?

options.A: Severe dehydration
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: Infection or inflammation

explanation: Great job! White blood cells are our body's soldiers. When they shoot up in number, it usually means they are busy fighting off an infection or inflammation.

question: What is a potential risk if a baby's skull undergoes excessive and very rapid moulding?

options.A: Permanent stunting of head growth after birth
options.B: Tearing of intracranial blood vessels
options.C: Complete blockage of cerebrospinal fluid pathways permanently
options.D: Premature fusion of the facial bones

explanation: While moulding is normal, if the bones shift too violently or fast, those delicate blood vessels inside can rupture. That's why monitoring labour progress is so important!

question: Which hormone directly triggers the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze milk out during the let-down reflex?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is the 'let-down' hormone. When the baby suckles, oxytocin makes the tiny muscle-like cells (myoepithelial cells) squeeze the milk down the ducts.

question: How does gender inequality directly contribute to early marriage?

options.A: By forcing boys to leave school early to work
options.B: By limiting educational opportunities for young girls
options.C: By granting young females absolute control over family assets
options.D: By making traditional marriage ceremonies illegal

explanation: When girls are denied education and future opportunities, society often pushes them straight into early marriage instead.

question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle much thicker than the right ventricle?

options.A: It receives blood directly from the lungs under high pressure.
options.B: It contracts more frequently than the right side of the heart.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of blood at rest.
options.D: It must pump blood through the entire systemic circulation.

explanation: Think of the left ventricle as the heavyweight champion of the heart. It needs extra muscle because it has to push blood all the way around your entire body!

question: Why is the "action line" on a partograph so critical for your clinical decisions?

options.A: It shows the exact moment the placenta will separate
options.B: It tells the nurse the baby's exact birth weight in grams
options.C: It signals that urgent medical intervention must be carried out
options.D: It proves that labour is proceeding much faster than average

explanation: When progress hits the action line, it's time to act! It means we need active steps like augmentation or surgery to keep everyone safe.

question: Which action best demonstrates effective psychosocial support by the nurse for a dying patient?

options.A: Leaving the room immediately when the patient starts crying
options.B: Telling the patient not to worry about the future
options.C: Sitting quietly by the bed and listening attentively to their concerns
options.D: Insisting that family members leave so the patient can rest

explanation: Active listening and quiet presence validate the patient's feelings and provide deep emotional comfort during a vulnerable time. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h4)

question: How do migrating cancer cells manage to break into nearby blood vessels?

options.A: They secrete enzymes that break down surrounding tissue barriers
options.B: They attract white blood cells to carry them into circulation
options.C: They wait for the blood vessel walls to rupture from high pressure
options.D: They shrink in size until they slip through normal cell walls

explanation: Spot on! Cancer cells release special chemical enzymes that chew through tissue barriers and blood vessel walls, letting them slip right into circulation.

question: Why would a patient need a triple-lumen catheter for continuous bladder irrigation?

options.A: It increases the French size automatically during surgery
options.B: It provides separate channels for drainage, balloon inflation, and fluid instillation
options.C: It prevents the patient from accidentally pulling the tube out
options.D: It allows three nurses to flush the bladder simultaneously

explanation: Exactly! Three separate pathways mean fluid can flow in, urine can flow out, and the balloon stays inflated all at the same time.

question: Why do we love using the metric system in healthcare?

options.A: Only international companies use it
options.B: It means no math is ever needed
options.C: Patients never ask questions about it
options.D: It uses a simple base-ten scale that makes conversions safe and easy

explanation: Base-ten means you can convert units just by moving the decimal point. No complicated math required!

question: What is the main reason a nurse asks a patient about a family history of blood disorders?

options.A: To predict the exact date the patient will recover
options.B: To find out if family members can pay for hospital bills
options.C: To identify inherited conditions passed down through genes
options.D: To determine which hospital room the patient prefers

explanation: Conditions like haemophilia and sickle cell disease are passed down from parents to children through genes. Family history is a great shortcut to knowing what to look out for!

question: What is the main focus of a nurse's day-to-day role in neurological care?

options.A: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders independently
options.B: Performing complex brain surgery in the theater
options.C: Prescribing long-term neurological medications
options.D: Protecting delicate brain and nerve tissue from further damage

explanation: You are on the front lines! Nurses play a vital role in preventing nervous system damage and protecting neural tissue before any permanent harm can happen.

question: When does the assessment of a patient's mental status actually begin?

options.A: Only after the deep tendon reflexes are completed
options.B: The moment you first greet and observe the patient
options.C: After the patient falls asleep for the night
options.D: When the laboratory blood work results return

explanation: Observation of appearance, alertness, and interaction starts immediately upon entering the room. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h5)

question: What happens to the follicular cells left behind in the ovary after ovulation?

options.A: They turn into permanent scar tissue
options.B: They turn into the corpus luteum and make progesterone
options.C: They travel down to meet the egg
options.D: They immediately dissolve and leave the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! The empty follicle gets a makeover into the corpus luteum, pumping out progesterone to get the uterus ready for a possible pregnancy.

question: Why do we use standard precautions in the hospital?

options.A: To treat active bacterial infections
options.B: To reduce the cost of patient care supplies
options.C: To prevent the transmission of infectious agents
options.D: To eliminate all microorganisms from the hospital environment

explanation: Spot on! Standard precautions are our everyday shield. By treating all body fluids as potentially infectious, we stop germs from spreading between patients and healthcare workers.

question: What is the primary danger of delaying or ignoring routine infrastructure maintenance in a hospital?

options.A: It always results in immediate promotion for the maintenance director
options.B: It forces the hospital to switch entirely to paperless documentation
options.C: It automatically increases the total number of available hospital beds
options.D: It can lead to equipment failure, safety hazards, and regulatory penalties

explanation: Putting off repairs creates hidden dangers that can harm patients or staff, and it leads to failing official health inspections. Keeping things fixed keeps everyone safe!

question: What happens when political pressure forces hospital managers to price drugs below what it costs to replace them?

options.A: Fund insolvency and complete stock depletion
options.B: Immediate intervention by international drug manufacturers
options.C: Rapid expansion of hospital infrastructure
options.D: Excessive profits for the pharmacy department

explanation: When prices drop too low due to pressure, you simply won't have enough money to buy new stock when the current batch runs out. That leads straight to empty pharmacy shelves!

question: Which health problem is a well-known long-term risk for patients taking steroids for a long time?

options.A: Chronic hypotension
options.B: Enhanced night vision
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Rapid weight loss

explanation: Long-term steroid use makes it harder for the body to absorb calcium and build strong bone, putting patients at higher risk for weak bones (osteoporosis).

question: Which sanitation practice helps stop rats and mice from taking over residential areas?

options.A: Storing harvested grains directly on bare dirt floors inside homes
options.B: Properly covering refuse bins and clearing overgrown bushes
options.C: Leaving domestic food waste uncovered in open backyard spaces
options.D: Digging shallow soakaway pits close to kitchen entrances

explanation: Spot on! Covering trash cuts off their food supply, and clearing bushes takes away their hiding spots.

question: Why are midwives particularly vital in Nigeria's primary health care system?

options.A: They focus solely on hospital administration and policy making
options.B: They handle only high-risk surgical emergencies in rural posts
options.C: They replace the need for community health extension workers entirely
options.D: They provide essential maternal care where specialized doctors are scarce

explanation: Primary health care centers rely heavily on midwives to deliver frontline maternal and child health services due to a shortage of obstetricians. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h1)
